h1:
Uttaradit Food
Best Eats in Town + Laplae
intro: Uttaradit is one of those drive-through towns most people zip straight past — but stop and eat here, and you'll find dishes you won't get anywhere else. Top of the list are khao pan phak (steamed veggie rolls) and mi pan from the town of Laplae, proper old-school local food, plus Northern dishes, seasonal fruit and some seriously good souvenirs. We've rounded up the places locals actually go.

blocks.html: Uttaradit and the district of Laplae are a pair you can eat your way through all day. The town itself has long-running spots for khao man kai (chicken rice), noodles and leng (pork blood and bone soup), while Laplae — about 8 kilometres out — is the home of khao pan phak and mi pan, local dishes you'll barely find sold anywhere else. We've sorted everything into sections so it's easy to plan your eating around your trip.

blocks.text: The dishes Laplae is known for

blocks.html: If you only eat one Laplae thing, make it khao pan phak. They spread a thin batter over a cloth stretched across a steaming pot, and once it sets they lay vegetables on top and roll it up, then ladle over broth or a house sauce. Mi pan is similar — a thin sheet wrapped around white noodles tossed with fish sauce, chilli flakes and lime. Light, fresh, and a hit with the health-conscious crowd.

items: Original khao pan phak — pure veggie rolls in a clear broth, easy to eat and the most traditional version.
Yen ta fo khao pan phak — drenched in pink yen ta fo broth, that sweet-sour balance that everyone ends up ordering.
Khao pan phak with red pork / braised beef — add roast pork or stewed beef when you want something more filling.
Mi pan — noodle salad wrapped in batter, lightly sour and spicy, the kind of thing you keep nibbling at.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.html: Most khao pan phak shops open from morning till early afternoon and make each roll to order. Weekends get busy and you may have to wait — if you'd rather not, get there before 11am.

blocks.text: Spots where the locals actually eat

blocks.html: Picked from places with a steady stream of real reviews on Wongnai and word of mouth from locals, mixing Laplae shops with spots in town and ordered so you can eat your way along the route. Prices are rough ranges and may shift with the menu and seasonal ingredients.

items.name: Phop Laplae Khao Pan Phak
items.blurb: The khao pan phak shop people think of first when they hit Laplae. It's on In Jai Mee Road, just before the Laplae town gate on the right, with plenty of toppings to choose from — clear broth, yen ta fo, red pork — all made fresh, one plate at a time.
items.meta: In Jai Mee Rd, before the Laplae gate · open morning–afternoon

items.name: Khao Pan Indy
items.blurb: A vintage-styled khao pan phak shop in Laplae that's nice to sit in. They do egg-wrapped khao pan phak, red pork khao pan phak, and yen ta fo egg rolls. Out-of-towners talk about this one a lot, and it photographs well too.

items.name: Pom Khao Pan Phak
items.blurb: A local shop that's been open for over 20 years. The standouts are the original khao pan phak, mi pan, and khao pan phak in suki and braised-pork flavours. Easy on the wallet, and a place Laplae folks have been eating at forever.

items.name: Lam Lam Laplae
items.blurb: A proper Northern restaurant in Laplae serving both khao pan phak and full khantoke-style Northern spreads. Good for when you want to sit down and order a bit of everything. Relaxed setting, open daily 10:00–20:00.

items.name: Hom Mali
items.blurb: A big place that does a bit of everything — Thai, Northern, Isan. What people order is the chicken massaman with Laplae durian, and the seasonal stir-fried hed phaw (earthball mushroom) curry. Air-conditioned room and a live-music area, great for a group.

items.name: Leng Lueat Mu (town)
items.blurb: A long-running leng (pork blood and bone soup) spot in town. Slurp the rich bone broth loaded with offal, with stewed pork leg to order on the side. A breakfast-to-late-morning meal locals come back to again and again.

items.name: Khao Man Kai Si Wai
items.blurb: A veteran chicken-rice shop near Seeharaj Hotel. They do both chicken rice and red pork rice at gentle prices — a simple, filling option for lunch in town.

items.name: By The River
items.blurb: A spot on the Nan River decked out with shipping containers, where you sit under a big tree by the water. The menu leans snacky-fusion — winged-bean salad, tom yum goong spaghetti, pork belly fried with fish sauce. Good for a chilled dinner.

blocks.html: Uttaradit sits on the seam between the lower North and the central plains, so its food carries a Northern accent with a central touch. If you want a serious Northern spread, places like Lam Lam Laplae and Hom Mali cover the lot — from nam prik num (young green chilli dip) and kaep mu (crispy pork rind) to seasonal local curries. The special thing here is the dishes that cook Laplae durian into savoury food, which is hard to find anywhere else.

items: Chicken massaman with Laplae durian — native durian goes into the curry for a sweet, rich local twist; only a few shops do it.
Stir-fried hed phaw curry — a rainy-season dish; fresh earthball mushrooms, crisp outside and soft within.
Nam prik & steamed-veg spread — nam prik num and nam prik ong eaten with local vegetables and crispy pork rind.
Khanom jeen nam ya / nam ngiao — local rice-noodle breakfasts you'll find at markets and shops around town.

blocks.title: Seasonal dishes
blocks.html: Dishes with durian or hed phaw mushrooms only show up when the local produce is in season. If you've really got your heart set on them, ask the shop first — out of season they usually won't have it.

Laplae is a genuine fruit town. The names to know are Long Laplae durian and Lin Laplae durian — small native durians weighing 1–2 kilos, with soft yellow flesh, slim seeds, a mild smell and a gentle sweetness. If strong durian odour usually puts you off, this is the one you can probably handle. Other local fruit includes langsat, hill longkong, and Huai Mun pineapple.

items: Long Laplae / Lin Laplae durian — around April–August; at peak everyone buys at the Hua Dong central fruit market.
Langsat — comes with the rainy season, sweet-tart with a thin skin.
Hill longkong from Laplae — around September–November, deep-flavoured with plenty of flesh and a thick skin.
Huai Mun pineapple — juicy, sweet and crisp, another local specialty.

blocks.title: Where to buy fruit
blocks.html: When durian is in, the Hua Dong municipal central fruit market is at its liveliest — fresh stock and several vendors competing on price, and you can usually taste before you buy. Come during the langsat-longkong festival (often held around September) and there's an especially big spread to choose from.
If you want to buy Laplae souvenirs, there's plenty locals love to carry back — from dry goods that keep for ages to local sweets. Pick based on who they're for and how far you're travelling.

items.name: Khao kaep
items.blurb: Sun-dried rice-flour sheets, a Laplae snack you grill or fry. Keeps for a long time and makes a classic souvenir.

items.name: Khanom thian sawoei
items.blurb: Laplae's own take on khanom thian — dense dough, packed filling. A well-known sweet that lots of people buy to take home.

items.name: Durian products
items.blurb: Durian paste, durian crisps, or Long Laplae durian ice cream — for anyone who wants that durian flavour in an easy-to-carry form.

items.name: Fresh seasonal fruit
items.blurb: Long Laplae durian, langsat, longkong — buy fresh from Hua Dong market, ideal if your trip home isn't far.

blocks.text: Plan a full day of eating in Uttaradit

blocks.html: With just one day you can do it comfortably by splitting the first half in town and the second half up in Laplae. Here's a meal-by-meal eating guide to follow.

items.activity: Start with leng pork soup or chicken rice in town
items.note: Town shops open early — slurp some warm broth before you set off.

items.activity: Drive up to Laplae (about 20 min) for khao pan phak at Phop Laplae or Pom
items.note: Get there before 11am to skip the queue; try both the clear broth and the yen ta fo.

items.activity: Stop at Hua Dong market for fruit, or sit at the Khao Pan Indy cafe
items.note: From April to August there's Long Laplae durian to taste.

items.activity: Finish with a Northern meal at Lam Lam Laplae, or sit by the water at By The River
items.note: Want a proper sit-down meal? Go Lam Lam. Want a chilled riverside vibe? By The River.

faq.q: What are the must-try foods in Uttaradit?
faq.a: Laplae's khao pan phak is the number one thing people think of — steamed batter rolled around vegetables, ladled with broth or yen ta fo. Next come mi pan, Northern food, and seasonal Long Laplae durian. These are local dishes that are hard to find outside the area.

faq.q: Where's the best place for khao pan phak in Laplae?
faq.a: The spots people mention most are Phop Laplae on In Jai Mee Road just before the town gate, the vintage-styled Khao Pan Indy that's nice to sit in, and Pom, which has been open for over 20 years. All three are cheap and made fresh to order — go before noon, as weekends get busy.

faq.q: When is Long Laplae durian in season?
faq.a: Long Laplae and Lin Laplae durian are out from around April to August each year, with the peak buying happening at the Hua Dong municipal central fruit market. Hill longkong from Laplae comes later, around September to November.

faq.q: What souvenirs can you buy in Uttaradit?
faq.a: The local souvenirs people carry back most are khao kaep, khanom thian sawoei, and durian products like durian paste or Long Laplae durian ice cream. If your trip home isn't far, buying fresh seasonal fruit from Hua Dong market is a great move too.

faq.q: Where can you eat Northern food in Uttaradit?
faq.a: Lam Lam Laplae does khantoke-style Northern food, while Hom Mali in town covers Thai, Northern and Isan, plus local-only dishes like chicken massaman with Laplae durian and seasonal hed phaw mushroom curry. Both are good for groups.
